name: Amariah
overview: Amariah was a male figure noted in Scripture as a descendant of Bani who had married a foreign wife. Beyond this unique attribute, there is little additional information about his tribe or other personal details. His mention is brief and specific to this genealogical and covenantal context.
namesAndTitles: The name Amariah is a proper name meaning 'YHWH has said.' This reveals a theophoric element, indicating a connection to the Lord's declaration or authority, though the name was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Amariah as a descendant of Bani, establishing a clear familial link. No other family relationships beyond this descent are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Amariah's significance lies in his inclusion among those who had intermarried with foreign wives, a matter addressed in the post-exilic community as they sought to maintain covenantal purity. His mention underscores the challenges faced by returning exiles in upholding God's commands and the importance of faithfulness to the covenant community.
